messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medvenue.com>, MedVenue Security Team <security@medvenue.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: MedVenue security discovery — subprocessor registry & data boundary follow-up

Hi Elena / MedVenue security team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — appreciate the thorough questions. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our end so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we covered
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (controls cover our hosted control plane and production inference runtime).
- Data handling: For hosted API customers MedVenue would use our multi-tenant hosted offering; customer data is isolated logically, and we accept contractual obligations for data residency where required.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud infra (CloudBridge), object storage for logs/backups, telemetry vendors for observability; we maintain a live subprocessor registry.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We support HIPAA-compliant deployments (BAA) and have data processing terms supporting GDPR obligations.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood to provide: current subprocessor roster + brief data flow notes (Jasmine) — by 2027-03-23 EOD
2) SOC 2 evidence (PDF certificate and SOC screencap) (Ben) — by 2027-03-23
3) Draft DPA/DPA redline path & DocuSign link (Legal / Marissa) — initial template by 2027-03-24
4) Follow-up 30-minute sync to go through any high-risk subprocessors and residency constraints (proposed window: week of 3/29) — propose times after you review the attachments

Attachments I will send in the follow-up: subprocessor roster CSV, SOC 2 certificate, and our DPA template (we'll attach as stubs in the next message).

If you want a narrower export of subprocessors limited to EU-only providers or a HIPAA-only view, tell me and we will filter accordingly.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medvenue.com>

Subject: Re: MedVenue security discovery — subprocessor registry & data boundary follow-up

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. A few follow-ups from the MedVenue security perspective: 

1) Please include the following fields in the subprocessor roster: vendor name, vendor contact, service provided, environment (prod/backup), data types accessed (PII/PHI/metadata), regions where data is stored, and whether the vendor is encrypted-at-rest/managed keys or customer-managed keys.

2) SOC 2: we need the latest Type II report or at minimum the certificate + SOC auditor contact for any verification call.

3) DPA / HIPAA: we will need a BAA in place for PHI processing. Please flag which subprocessors are engaged in PHI processing so we can escalate those for legal review.

4) Cloud partners: you mentioned CloudBridge during the call; can you provide the contract tier (managed VMs vs. dedicated instances) and whether Redwood uses customer-dedicated tenancy for enterprise (if available). Also need confirmation of whether logs containing request metadata are ever forwarded to a third-party analytics vendor.

5) Can you also provide an estimated timeline for any on-prem/private deployment (MedVenue is exploring a private deployment later this year but needs to understand feasibility and lead times).

If you can send the roster and SOC artifacts by Wednesday EOD (3/23) that would help us triage the high-risk vendors quickly.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Director, Information Security
MedVenue Health
elena.rossi@medvenue.com

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Please find the initial artifacts attached and short answers inline below. Happy to jump on a call to walk through anything.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_2027-03-21.csv (columns: vendor name, contact, service, environment, data types accessed, regions, encryption/key mgmt, PHI flag)
- redwood_soc2_type2_certificate_2026.pdf (certificate + auditor contact included)
- redwood_dpa_template_2027.docx (DocuSign-ready DPA)

Quick answers to your bullets:
- CloudBridge (primary infra): we run on CloudBridge managed instances by default for hosted customers. For enterprise customers we offer dedicated tenancy and dedicated capacity pools via Redwood Dedicated (requires contract addendum).
- Logs / analytics: request metadata (non-PII request IDs, latency metrics) is retained for operational analytics. We do not forward PHI to external analytics vendors. Any telemetry sent to our observability partner is filtered to exclude content-level fields; request text is redacted for customers that elect stricter controls.
- PHI subprocessors: in this roster we flagged two vendors that can handle PHI when customers opt-in for extended logging: CloudBridge (managed infra for backups), SecureVault (encrypted backup provider). Both are flagged in the PHI column.
- On-prem/private timeline: typical delivery for Private (VPC + customer-managed KMS) is 8–12 weeks after SOW sign; can expedite in some enterprise cases with dedicated engineering resource.

Next steps: please review the attachments and let us know which vendors you want escalated; we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up the week of 3/29 — suggested windows attached in HubSpot.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
